frames.narration: A big seller's import of 100,000 photos is in the bulk lane, and the autoscaler has raised the fleet to cope. Another seller adds a photo to a listing. The app asks the upload API for permission; the API records photo p-81 as pending.
The API returns a signed URL for one key, valid for a few minutes and up to 20 MB. The app uploads straight to object storage and shows its local copy on the listing meanwhile.
Storage announces the new object, and because a person is waiting for it the job goes to the interactive lane, not behind the import.
A worker always checks the interactive lane first. It reads the header (3,000 by 4,000 pixels, a real JPEG, under the pixel limit), then decodes it in a sandbox with a memory and time limit.

It writes 6 variants under names built from the original's hash, the size and format, and the pipeline version, each to a temporary key renamed when complete. Then it moves p-81 to ready with a conditional write. If this job ran twice, it would write the same 6 files.
Between interactive jobs the same workers take photos from the bulk lane, so the import keeps moving without ever getting in front of a seller who is waiting.

A buyer opens the listing. The browser asks for the 640 px WebP; the CDN misses once, fetches it from storage and caches it for a year, since the name never changes meaning. About 8 seconds after the seller tapped upload, the photo is live.

Months later the store adds a 1,200 px size. A buyer asks for it before the backfill has reached p-81, so the resizer makes it from the original on the spot, stores it, and the CDN caches it. The slow backfill will skip p-81 now that it exists.
